rows.note: Use 或者 as the all-purpose choice for ordinary alternatives, including alternative names.

example.english: You can call me Ah Ming or Ah Man.
example.traditional: 你可以叫我阿明或者阿文。
example.jyutping: nei5 ho2 ji5 giu3 ngo5 aa3 ming4 waak6 ze2 aa3 man4

rows.note: Use 定係 especially when asking someone to choose between alternatives.

example.english: Do you want to eat at a cha chaan teng or have Japanese food?
example.traditional: 你想食茶餐廳定係日本菜？
example.jyutping: nei5 soeng2 sik6 caa4 caan1 teng1 ding6 hai6 jat6 bun2 coi3

rows.note: Use 唔係就 after a warning or condition to mean that otherwise a consequence will follow.

example.english: Leave now, or you won't make it in time.
example.traditional: 快啲走，唔係就趕唔切喇。
example.jyutping: faai3 di1 zau2 m4 hai6 zau6 gon2 m4 cit3 laa3

rows.note: Use 又叫 when introducing another equivalent name for the same person, place, or thing.

example.english: Hong Kong is also called Xianggang, or the Fragrant Harbour.
example.jyutping: hoeng1 gong2 jau6 giu3 hoeng1 gong1
